toegepas.voor: Soutwater bevat baie sout en ons vind
toegepas.na: Soutwater bevat baie sout, en ons vind
toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS 2017: two clauses each with their own subject and verb (Soutwater bevat / ons vind) take a comma before en.
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS comma between two main clauses (Soutwater bevat / ons vind).
toegepas.rede_keurder: Each clause has its own subject and verb, so AWS 2017 requires the comma; no words added.

toegepas.voor: Daar is wel 'n bietjie sout in, maar te min om sout te proe.
toegepas.na: Daar is wel 'n bietjie sout daarin, maar te min om dit te proe.
toegepas.rede_vinder: The stranded 'in' is spoken style and repeating 'sout' is wooden; 'daarin' and 'dit' read more naturally with the same meaning.
toegepas.fout: Stranded 'in' after existential 'daar' reads as spoken style, and 'sout' is repeated woodenly.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'daarin' and 'dit' read naturally, the word count is unchanged, and 'dit' can only mean the salt, so the meaning stays.

toegepas.na: vleilande. Daar is ook varswater in ys
toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS 2017 puts no comma before en in a list, and without it the long list of places runs on; a new sentence keeps every place and leaves the protected wording intact.
toegepas.fout: Comma before 'en' inside a list of places, against AWS 2017, in an overlong sentence.
toegepas.rede_keurder: A real punctuation fault; the new sentence keeps every place and leaves the protected 'die meeste mere en die meeste vleilande' intact, so the two added words are justified.

toegepas.voor: lê in die oseane en daardie water is sout
toegepas.na: lê in die oseane, en daardie water is sout
toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS 2017: two clauses each with their own subject and verb take a comma before en.
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS comma between two main clauses (water le / daardie water is).
toegepas.rede_keurder: Both halves are full clauses with their own subject and verb, so the comma is required.

toegepas.voor: Die son maak die water warm en van die water
toegepas.na: Die son maak die water warm, en van die water
toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS 2017: two clauses each with their own subject and verb (Die son maak / van die water verander) take a comma before en.
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS comma between two main clauses (Die son maak / van die water verander).
toegepas.rede_keurder: Each clause has its own subject and verb, so AWS 2017 requires the comma.

toegepas.rede_vinder: 'dit' points back to the waterdamp of the previous sentence, so the sentence reads as if water vapour is called evaporation; naming the change (from 'verander in waterdamp') fixes the reference.
toegepas.fout: 'dit' points back to 'waterdamp' (the previous sentence's 'jy kan dit nie sien nie'), so the sentence reads as if water vapour is called evaporation.
toegepas.rede_keurder: A real reference fault on a key term; 'hierdie verandering' points to the change into vapour, which is what evaporation is, at the cost of one word.

toegepas.voor: seewater warm en van daardie water
toegepas.na: seewater warm, en van daardie water
toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS 2017: two clauses each with their own subject and verb (Die son maak / van daardie water verdamp) take a comma before en.
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS comma between two main clauses (Die son maak / van daardie water verdamp).
toegepas.rede_keurder: Each clause has its own subject and verb, so AWS 2017 requires the comma.

toegepas.voor: en bly agter in die see
toegepas.na: en bly in die see agter
toegepas.rede_vinder: The separable verb agterbly puts its particle at the end of the clause in natural Afrikaans.
toegepas.fout: 'bly agter in die see' can be misread as 'at the back of the sea' and leaves the particle of 'agterbly' mid-clause.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'bly in die see agter' is the natural order and removes the misreading without changing meaning or length.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The separable verb opstyg puts its particle at the end of the clause in natural Afrikaans; 'styg op in die lug' follows English word order.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'styg op in die lug' is a natural Afrikaans placement of the prepositional phrase after the particle and is not ambiguous, so the proposal is a lateral move.

laat_vaar.voor: Na 'n ruk is die water weg en lê daar
laat_vaar.na: Na 'n ruk is die water weg, en lê daar
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: AWS 2017: each clause has its own subject and verb (die water is / 'n wit lagie lê); the reviewer may judge the shared opening 'Na 'n ruk' makes it one sentence and drop this.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Both clauses hang on the shared opener 'Na 'n ruk' (hence the inverted 'le daar'), so it is one sentence and a comma would split the shared element.

na_skrywer.voor: Water met baie sout in, soos
na_skrywer.na: Water wat baie sout bevat, soos
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: The stranded 'in' is spoken style; 'wat baie sout bevat' is standard written Afrikaans and matches the varswater entry beside it.
na_skrywer.fout: The glossary entry 'Water met baie sout in' ends in a spoken-style stranded 'in' and does not match the parallel varswater entry ('wat baie min sout bevat').
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: A real style fault, but it rewords a shared glossary definition beyond a plain grammar or spelling error, so only the writer may change it, for every lesson at once.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

vlae.teks: Water verdamp ook uit riviere, damme, nat grond en die see.
vlae.rede: The protected wording is 'Water verdamp ook uit riviere, damme, nat grond en plante', but the lesson ends the list with 'die see' and has no 'plante'. The protected sentence does not occur in the lesson, so either the lesson or the protected entry is out of date; this is content, so it was not changed.

beskerm_bedenkings.woord: Water verdamp ook uit riviere, damme, nat grond en plante
beskerm_bedenkings.rede: This protected wording does not appear in the lesson as written (the lesson has 'nat grond en die see'), so it protects nothing here; a person should check which version is intended.
